questions.q: The equivalent resistance of the circuit shown below between points $a$ and $b$ is :

The resistance in& $ab$~is parallel to all other resistances. Since all the resistances other than~${R}_{b}$~is~$4Ω$~the potential is zero \left({V}_{x} = {V}_{y}\right)$ as the upper branch will become a case of balanced wheatstone bridge between~${V}_{x} \text{ and } {V}_{y}$. questions.q: A teacher in his physics laboratory allotted an experiment to determine the resistance  \left(G\right)$ a galvanometer. Students took the observations for $\dfrac{1}{3}$ deflection in the galvanometer. Which of the below is true for measuring value of $G$?$
options: $\dfrac{1}{3}$ deflection method cannot be used for determining the resistance of the galvanometer.
$\dfrac{1}{3}$~deflection method can be used and in this case the $G$ equals to twice the value of shunt resistance(s).
$\dfrac{1}{3}$ deflection method can be used and in this case, the G equals to three times the value of shunt resistance(s).
$\dfrac{1}{3}$ deflection method can be used and in this case the $G$ value equals to the shunt resistance(s)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If a large resistance $R$~is connected with a battery, then current will be approximately $\dfrac{ε}{R}$, and $t$ will remain almost constant.

In ${1}^{st}$ case, only \left(G\right)$ is connected $⇒ ig = i$

In ${2}^{nd}$ case,

${i}_{g}{R}_{0} = \left(I - {i}_{g}\right)S ⇒ \left({i}_{g}\right)2 = \left(\dfrac{S}{{R}_{g} + S}\right)i$

If \left({i}_{g}\right)2 = \dfrac{1}{3}\left({i}_{g}\right), ⇒ \left(\dfrac{S}{{R}_{g} + S}\right)i = \dfrac{1}{3}i$

${R}_{g} = 2S

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I : The equivalent resistance of resistors in a series combination is smaller than least resistance used in the combination.

Statement II : The resistivity of the material is independent of temperature. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are false
Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are true
Statement $I$ is true but Statement $II$ is false
Statement $I$ is false but Statement $II$ is true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula for series equivalent resistance is given by&

${R}_{s} = {R}_{1} + {R}_{2} + . . . . . . + {R}_{n}$.~

Hence, the equivalent resistance will be the highest value compared to other resistances.

The resistivity of a material is given by,

$ρ = {ρ}^{0} \left(1 + \alpha\Delta T\right)

Clearly, the resistivity is dependant on temperature.

Hence, this is the right option.

$

questions.q: Two identical heater filaments are connected first in parallel and then in series. At the same applied voltage, the ratio of heat produced in same time for parallel to series will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the resistance of the filaments be& $R$~and the voltage be~$V$.

For the series combination the power is~

${P}_{1} = \left(\dfrac{V2}{2R}\right)~

For parallel combination,

${P}_{2} = V^{2} \left(\dfrac{R}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{2V^{2}}{R}\right)

Hence, the ratio is

$⇒ \dfrac{P2}{P1} = \dfrac{4}{1}$

questions.q: Wheatstone bridge principle is used to measure the specific resistance  \left({S}_{1}\right)$ of given wire, having length $L$, radius $r$. If $X$ is the resistance of wire, then specific resistance is : ${S}_{1} = X \left(\dfrac{\pir^{2}}{L}\right).$If the length of the wire gets doubled then the value of specific resistance will be :$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The specific resistance of a material, also known as electrical resistivity, is a measure of how strongly a specific material opposes the flow of electric current.

Specific resistance is an intrinsic property of a material and is dependent on factors such as the material's composition, temperature, and crystal structure. It is the counterpart of conductivity, with which it is inversely proportional.

Hence, even if the length of the wire is doubled, the specific resistance remains the same, i.e., ${S}_{1}$.

Given below are two statements :

Statement II : Two resistance $2R$ and $3R$ are connected in parallel in an electric circuit. The value of thermal energy developed in $3R$ and $2R$ will be in the ratio $3: 2$.

options: Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The work done in stopping the car and the truck can be written as

$\begin{cases}W & = & Fx \\ & = & ∆ KE\end{cases}$

As both the car and the truck are moving initially with the same kinetic energy, after being stopped, they will have the same change of kinetic energy.

Also, they are stopped with the same applied force.

Hence, from the above equation, it can be written that~they have the same displacement, i.e.,~${x}_{1} = {x}_{2}$.

Acceleration is a vector quantity. As the direction of motion of the car is different in the two given situations, the acceleration of the car will not be the same.

questions.q: A cell of internal resistance $r$ drives current through an external resistance $R .$ The power delivered by the cell to the external resistance will be maximum when:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Current $i = \dfrac{E}{r + R}$
Power generated in $R$

$P = i^{2}R$
$P = \dfrac{E^{2}R}{( r + R{)}^{2}}$

for maximum power $\dfrac{dP}{dR} = 0$
$E^{2}\left[\dfrac{( r + R{)}^{2} \times 1 - R \times 2 ( r + R )}{( r + R{)}^{4}}\right] = 0$
$⇒ \text{when,}r = R\text{then,}\dfrac{dP}{dR} = 0$

questions.q: Eight copper wire of length $l$ and diameter d are joined in parallel to form a single composite conductor of resistance $R$. If a single copper wire of length $2l$ have the same resistance  \left(R\right)$ then its diameter will be _____~$d$.$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Each wire has resistance,& $r = ρ\dfrac{4l}{\pid^{2}}$

Eight wire in parallel, then equivalent resistance is

$R = \dfrac{r}{8} = \dfrac{ρl}{2\pid^{2}}$

Single copper wire of length $2l$ has resistance~$R = ρ\dfrac{2l \times 4}{\pi{d}_{1}^{2}}$.

Comparing both equations,~we get,

$ρ\dfrac{8l}{\pi{d}_{1}^{2}} = \dfrac{ρl}{2\pid^{2}}$

$⇒ {d}_{1} = 4d$

questions.q: In the circuit diagram shown in figure given below, the current flowing through resistance $3Ω$~is $\dfrac{x}{3}A$. The value of $x$ is ________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the current flowing through the circuit be& $IA$~in anti-clockwise direction.

The net resistance is~$R = 4 . 5Ω + 2Ω + 1 . 5Ω = 8Ω$

Hence,~$I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{4V}{8Ω} = 0 . 5A$

The current flowing through the~$3Ω$~resistor is~

$\dfrac{6}{6 + 3} \times 0 . 5 = \dfrac{1}{3}A$

So,~$x = 1$
